messages:
Carlos: Quick heads-up — NexaSupply just pushed our H100 replen shipment by ~3 weeks due to a customs backlog in FRA. They also flagged possible AWB consolidations that could delay some serials. Need to coordinate provisioning, RMA pre-auth, and any routing changes. Anyone blocking eu-west-1 large pools?
Raj: Ack. Do we have the new ETA exact date? Impact on committed Dedicated pools?
Nina (VendorBot): NexaSupply update for order 8675309: status=delayed; ETA 2026-04-12 -> 2026-05-03; RMA window=10d after delivery; note: FRA customs backlog severity=medium-high. See vendor portal: https://vendor.nexa/ord/8675309
Mei: We saw similar consolidation last quarter — crossdock option reduced transit time but added a 48h customs inspection risk. If they force AWB merge, serial split may happen and we'll need temporary serial mapping for staging.
Carlos: That ETA shift would nudge our eu capacity start that's pinned to Dedicated commits. Priya — what does cluster demand look like in next 4 weeks?
Priya: If deliveries move to May, capacity shortfall ~18% for eu-west-1 reserved pools. Non-critical batch jobs can be throttled; recommend enabling burst policy to g4-like nodes in cloud for 2-3 weeks. Also we should pre-authorize RMA crossdock to avoid depot wait.
Raj: Agree on burst fallback. Also networking: our backhaul links into FRA DC are at 85% utilization during peak window; any reroute to AMS will add an extra 40ms p95 for intra-region traffic. Is that tolerable?
Mei: OPS note — if we reroute to AMS we need new forwarder slots and a different customs broker (they charge ~€200 additional per AWB). I'll check fast quotes but we need procurement sign-off.
Carlos: Procurement: can we accept broker cost for critical pool? Otherwise we delay and risk SLO breaches.
Raj: Small config snippet to enable burst fallback (Devex asked to keep this handy):
```json
{
  "pool": "eu-west-1-dedicated-1",
  "fallback": [{"provider":"cloud-g4","max_instances":20,"priority":50}],
  "throttle_noncritical": true
}
```
Mei: For RMA logistics: propose pre-creating a crossdock manifest template and pre-authorizing temporary serial mapping for up to 200 nodes. That'll let us accept split AWBs without manual reconcile.
Carlos: Sounds good. Mei — please draft the manifest template and list the KYC docs vendor will need. Raj/Priya — can you assess SLO risk if we enable the cloud fallback?
Priya: Quick risk calc: fallback + throttle reduces customer-facing latency impact to <5% for 2-3 weeks; cost delta ~+12% for that period. If we use cached KV prefix trick we can shave token cost a bit.
Raj: Note: if we enable fallback, update rate limiter policy to avoid bursting too many long-running generative jobs.
Mei: Manifest draft attached (will upload to the ring after this thread). Also asked Nexa to confirm whether AWB merges will preserve original serials in the manifest — vendor replied: "we will provide mapping CSV if split occurs".
Nina (VendorBot): NexaSupply message received: "We will provide AWB->serial mapping CSV within 24h of manifest creation. RMA pick window extends by 48h if crossdock used."
Carlos: Ok — action items: 1) Mei: draft manifest + cost estimate for AMS broker. 2) Procurement: sign off on up to €200/AWB if needed. 3) Raj/Priya: prepare config change to enable fallback + rate-limit update; dry-run deploy to staging. 4) Ops: pre-authorize RMA crossdock for up to 200 serials.
Raj: I can prep the staging dry-run today.
Mei: I'll send manifest + cost in next 2 hours.
Priya: I'll run the SLO sims and post numbers here within 6h.
OpsBot: Reminder: scheduled maintenance window tonight 23:00-01:00 UTC — if you push pool config changes, mark as emergency-only.
Carlos: Thanks team. We'll triage in the 11:30 PT sync if any blockers remain. :thumbsup:
